## Summary
- Add `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE` and a deterministic `agent-self-merge.yml` workflow/CLI.
- Route `agent-self-approve -> approved` to self-merge only when self-merge is enabled, while preserving disabled stop behavior and `REQUEST_CHANGES -> fix-pr`.
- Verify open non-draft PRs, current-head Sepo self-approval, no blocking requested changes, check/mergeability state, and default-branch base safety before merging or enabling auto-merge.
- Add marker-upserted self-merge statuses, docs, and focused regression tests.

## Verification
- `npm run build`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/self-merge.test.js dist/__tests__/resolve-self-merge-cli.test.js dist/__tests__/handoff.test.js dist/__tests__/orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.js dist/__tests__/orchestrator-preflight-cli.test.js dist/__tests__/sub-orchestration.test.js dist/__tests__/post-response-cli.test.js dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #200

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #202 implements issue #200, the self-merge slice under parent issue #170.
- It adds an opt-in `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE` gate, deterministic resolver/CLI/workflow, orchestration routing from self-approval, docs, and focused tests.
- The intended behavior is to merge only a currently self-approved PR head, enable auto-merge when appropriate, and wait visibly for stacked PR bases.
- The PR is stacked on PR #186, and issue #200 explicitly required PR #186 to be refreshed onto the latest PR #184 head before this slice proceeded.

## Review
The reviewers generally agree the implementation shape is strong: the self-merge flow is deterministic, gated, documented, and well covered. Two unresolved issues remain: one is a trust-boundary race in the merge command, and the other is the unmet stacked-base prerequisite.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Merge command can race past the approved head | BLOCKING | The resolver verifies current-head self-approval, but `gh pr merge` is called without `--match-head-commit`, so a push after preflight could merge or enable auto-merge for an unapproved head. |
| Stacked base was not refreshed as requested | BLOCKING | Issue #200 required PR #186 to be refreshed onto the latest PR #184 head first; PR #186 still points at the old #184 base, and PR #202 is stacked on that stale PR. |

## Progress
- Rubrics review already acknowledged the stack-refresh gap as partial compliance.
- Existing inline review comments were empty before synthesis.
- Posted one new inline comment on [`.agent/src/github.ts` line 321](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/202#discussion_r3215400413).
- No replies were added and no existing comments were minimized.
- Optional polish notes from one reviewer, such as merge-method configurability and immediate-merge status visibility, are not treated as required action items.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Merge command can race past the approved head</summary>

**Cause:** [`mergePullRequest` and `enablePullRequestAutoMerge`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/77a99f1c0786223847b4ce7989241fdf1c03b957/.agent/src/github.ts#L320-L325) merge by PR number only. The verified head SHA from preflight is not passed into the final mutation.

**Candidate solutions:** Thread the verified PR head SHA into both merge helpers and call `gh pr merge ... --match-head-commit <sha>` for immediate merge and auto-merge. Add CLI coverage asserting the fake `gh` command receives the flag.

**Comments:** This is the highest-risk finding because it undermines the current-head self-approval guarantee.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Stacked base was not refreshed as requested</summary>

**Cause:** Issue #200 explicitly says PR #186 should be refreshed onto the latest PR #184 head before this slice proceeds. Live metadata shows PR #184 head is `e5fc865406f35cd15c713bb346e1149b5b9e4263`, while PR #186 is still based on old #184 base `406289094cf4ddef7a8c4b3dea98b48dc2f756ea`; PR #202 is then stacked on PR #186.

**Candidate solutions:** Refresh PR #186 onto current PR #184, then rebase or refresh PR #202 onto the updated PR #186 and rerun the targeted verification.

**Comments:** Reviewers differed on severity, but this synthesis treats it as blocking because it was an explicit prerequisite in the issue task.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: unresolved findings require concrete branch changes and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
`NEEDS_REWORK`

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #202 implements issue #200, the self-merge slice under parent issue #170.
- It adds an opt-in `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE` gate, deterministic self-merge CLI/workflow behavior, orchestration routing from `agent-self-approve -> approved`, docs, and focused tests.
- The core safety goal is to merge or enable auto-merge only for a PR head that Sepo has self-approved at the current commit.
- The earlier stacked-base prerequisite has now been satisfied: PR #186 is based on current PR #184 head `e5fc8654`, and PR #202 is based on refreshed PR #186 head `f3a76156`.

## Review
The reviewers agree the design is mostly sound and the stack refresh is now fixed. One blocking trust-boundary issue remains: the final merge mutation is still not bound to the approved head SHA.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Merge command can race past the approved head | BLOCKING | [`mergePullRequest` and `enablePullRequestAutoMerge`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/a54e3dbc708403c3279d675b84a3feb0e504bed1/.agent/src/github.ts#L320-L325) call `gh pr merge` without `--match-head-commit`, so a push after preflight could merge or auto-merge an unapproved head. |
| Immediate self-merge success has no Sepo status comment | WARNING | `status_post` is false for `conclusion === "merged"`, so immediate merges lack the same Sepo-authored PR-thread status that other outcomes get. |
| Empty merge state is treated as auto-merge-safe | WARNING | `canEnableAutoMerge` allows `mergeStateStatus === ""`, which is an indeterminate state rather than a known safe merge state. |
| Blocked self-merge terminal mapping lacks direct coverage | INFO | `SELF_MERGE_TERMINAL_STATES` maps `blocked -> blocked`, but the direct `resultStateFromTerminal` test coverage only exercises other self-merge conclusions. |

## Progress
- The stack-refresh action item from the earlier synthesis is fixed.
- The latest rubrics review and both reviewer outputs still flag the missing `--match-head-commit` guard.
- Existing inline comment [#discussion_r3215400413](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/202#discussion_r3215400413) already covers the blocking line-specific issue and is still current on head `a54e3dbc`.
- No new inline comments were posted, no replies were added, and no comments were minimized during this synthesis.
- Optional UX/test-hardening warnings are noted but kept out of required automation action items.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Merge command can race past the approved head</summary>

**Cause:** The CLI verifies `meta.headOid` has a current-head self-approval, but the later mutation calls `mergePullRequest(prNumber, repo)` or `enablePullRequestAutoMerge(prNumber, repo)` without passing that verified SHA. The helpers then run `gh pr merge` by PR number only.

**Candidate solutions:** Thread the verified head SHA into both helpers and call `gh pr merge ... --match-head-commit <sha>` for immediate merge and auto-merge. Update the CLI tests to assert the fake `gh` log includes `--match-head-commit`.

**Comments:** This is the only required blocker. It undermines the core current-head self-approval guarantee.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Immediate self-merge success has no Sepo status comment</summary>

**Cause:** [`resolve-self-merge.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/a54e3dbc708403c3279d675b84a3feb0e504bed1/.agent/src/cli/resolve-self-merge.ts#L148-L152) sets `status_post` to false when the conclusion is `merged`.

**Candidate solutions:** Either post the same compact status body for `merged`, or document that successful immediate merges rely on GitHub’s merge event and workflow artifact.

**Comments:** This is product/UX judgment, not required for the fix-pr pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Empty merge state is treated as auto-merge-safe</summary>

**Cause:** `canEnableAutoMerge` permits an empty normalized merge state, which can mean merge state was unavailable rather than acceptable.

**Candidate solutions:** Remove `""` from the allowed merge states, or require an explicit acceptable `mergeable` value before enabling auto-merge.

**Comments:** One reviewer flagged this as slightly permissive; no reviewer treated it as blocking.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Blocked self-merge terminal mapping lacks direct coverage</summary>

**Cause:** The new sub-orchestration mapping includes `blocked`, but direct tests cover `merged`, `auto_merge_enabled`, `waiting`, and `failed`.

**Candidate solutions:** Add one focused `resultStateFromTerminal` assertion for `agent-self-merge` with `blocked`.

**Comments:** Existing handoff coverage reduces risk, so this is informational.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: the remaining blocker is a scoped code/test change that automation can safely apply.

## Final Verdict
`NEEDS_REWORK`

**Comments:** This is a product/UX decision, not a correctness blocker.

**Comments:** Existing handoff and structurally similar marker coverage reduce risk.

this becomes way much more complicated than I expected. I think is just simple: when we have agent self approve passed the check, then we can just merge this PR?

Yes, that is the intended simple behavior for a normal PR:

`review SHIP -> agent-self-approve approves current head -> checks/mergeability pass -> agent-self-merge merges`.

The extra logic in #202 is mostly guardrails around that simple rule. The resolver only merges when self-merge is enabled, the PR is open and non-draft, the base is the default branch, the current head has Sepo’s self-approval for that exact SHA, there are no requested changes, checks are not failing, and GitHub reports it mergeable. See [`self-merge.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/daee1f9c7fe9e671688b32d0f1d3cbbbf97e71ad/.agent/src/self-merge.ts#L197-L313). The actual merge command is also bound to the approved head with `--match-head-commit`, so a later push cannot sneak through after approval: [`github.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/daee1f9c7fe9e671688b32d0f1d3cbbbf97e71ad/.agent/src/github.ts#L326-L350).

For this PR specifically: #202’s latest check is passing, and the latest review synthesis says no required code changes remain. But it is still a draft and is stacked on #186, not the default branch. Under the implementation in this PR, self-merge would wait/block in that state rather than merge. The practical next step is: mark #202 ready when you accept the optional warnings, then merge the stack in order or let self-merge handle PRs once they are based on the default branch and have current-head self-approval.

@sepo-agent /answer

You’re right. The current #202 policy is too conservative for how this repo actually works.

The safety rule should not be “non-draft + default branch only.” It should be closer to:

`current-head self-approval + checks/mergeability pass + no requested changes + approved head still matches -> merge into the PR’s configured base`

That means two changes to #202’s design:

1. **Draft agent PRs should be eligible**
   - Agent-created PRs are commonly draft during automation.
   - Once `agent-self-approve` has approved the exact current head and checks pass, draft status should not be a terminal blocker.
   - The self-merge workflow can deterministically mark the PR ready before merging, but only for trusted agent PRs/branches.

2. **Stacked PRs should be mergeable into their base branch**
   - The current default-branch guard in [`self-merge.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/daee1f9c7fe9e671688b32d0f1d3cbbbf97e71ad/.agent/src/self-merge.ts#L254-L260) would block normal stacked agent PRs.
   - For this repo, if #202 is based on #186’s branch, self-merge should be allowed to merge #202 into #186’s branch after the same approval/check/head guards pass.
   - We still need to reject unsafe bases, such as fork bases or unknown branches, but not same-repo stacked agent bases.

I’d revise #202 with a small follow-up fix:

- Replace the draft hard block with “draft is allowed for trusted agent PRs; mark ready before merge.”
- Replace the default-branch-only guard with “allow default branch or same-repo PR stack base.”
- Keep the important guards: `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE`, current-head self-approval, no requested changes, green/pending checks handling, mergeability, and `--match-head-commit`.

So yes: your simpler model is the right product behavior. The implementation should support the repo’s actual workflow: agent draft PRs and stacked PRs are first-class, not exceptions.
